column1: 74 sites · multi-vendor DCS (Honeywell / Emerson / Yokogawa / Foxboro / Matrikon; future ABB / GE) · Edge-to-Broker architecture · No DCOM / No OPC Tunneler.  Questions to be issued to PDO and Yokogawa.  Addressee: P = PDO, Y = Yokogawa, B = Both.

column3: Question / Clarification Required
column4: Why It Matters (Rationale)
column7: Response (to be completed by PDO / Yokogawa)

column3: The spec references integration with AVEVA System Platform / Wonderware (rows 17, 29, 30) and a System Platform tag-count impact (row 53), yet the current direction(as pe the dicussion yesterday with Mr. Girish) indicates this may be descoped in favour of standalone operator stations. Please confirm definitively: is AVEVA System Platform / IOC SCADA integration IN or OUT of scope?
column4: This single answer reshapes the client UI, the licensing model and the System Platform tag-count requirement. It is the largest open variable in the design.

column3: Confirm the total number of DCS / OPC source systems across the 74 sites, broken down by OEM (Honeywell / Emerson / Yokogawa / Foxboro / Matrikon / other).
column4: Drives the number of edge collectors, connector licences and total integration effort.

column3: Are all 74 sites on one common PCD / OT network, or distributed across remote WAN links into the IOC? Please provide the network topology between sites, the CCR and the IOC.
column4: Determines whether edge collectors publish to a single broker or to regional aggregation brokers, and the bandwidth/latency budget.

column3: To honour 'No DCOM and No OPC Tunneler', our edge-to-broker model needs the edge collector to run locally alongside each OPC A&E source (local COM, no remote DCOM). Are we permitted to install our lightweight edge agent directly on the existing OEM OPC A&E server or in a separate machine in the same layer?
column4: Local installation is the direct technical consequence of the No-DCOM rule.

column3: If installing third-party software on the existing OPC server VM/server machine is prohibited by OEM warranty or PCD policy, what is the approved topology for local extraction — e.g. will PDO provision an adjacent VM/Server on the identical local subnet so the OPC connection remains local within the same layer?
column4: If we cannot co-reside on the OPC server machine, PDO must provision adjacent edge server/VM

column3: Please confirm acceptance of the edge-to-broker pattern (MQTT / Sparkplug B over TLS) as the PCD-to-IOC transport, replacing DCOM and OPC tunnelling.
column4: Confirms the foundational transport choice satisfies the No-DCOM/No-Tunneler requirement and cyber policy.

column3: Spec requires a 'single string per OPC A&E server'. Confirm this means one A&E subscription session per server, filtered at the edge — not per-tag DA polling.
column4: Confirms the low-load, event-driven A&E subscription model the spec intends and avoids OPC-server overload.

column3: Is deployment of Docker / Kubernetes (containerization) officially approved and supported within the PDO PCD?
column4: Modern brokered architectures often containerize. the answer dictates the deployment model.

column3: If containers are not approved, confirm we are limited to PDO-provided Windows Server / Linux VMs for the broker and central services, and state the standard OS builds/versions available.
column4: Locks the supported deployment platform and OS baseline for sizing and compatibility.

column3: What CPU / RAM / disk resources are available on the OPC A&E VMs (or adjacent edge VMs) to host the edge agent and buffer store-and-forward data during outages?
column4: Required to size the local buffer for the mandated store-and-forward / backfill capability.

column3: Will PDO provide the central / IOC compute (VMs, storage, database hosting), or must it be included in our offer?
column4: Determines hardware scope and pricing for the central tier.

column3: Confirm the virtualization/hypervisor standard in the PCD and IOC (VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, etc.) and any mandated hardening baseline
column4: Ensures our components are certified/supported on the target platform and meet hardening rules.

column3: Is there a DMZ between the PCD/CCR and the IOC? Please provide the Purdue-level segmentation and the security zones the solution must traverse.
column4: Defines where the broker bridge and any DMZ-resident services sit, and how many zone boundaries data crosses.

column3: If acknowledgment from the IOC is required, can firewalls permit the specific bidirectional edge-to-broker path, or must acknowledgment be local-only at the DCS?
column4: Confirms whether a controlled return channel is allowed or whether ack stays at the DCS.

column3: Which secure protocols and ports are approved by PDO cybersecurity for edge-to-broker traffic (e.g. MQTT over TLS 1.2/1.3 on port 8883)?
column4: Firewall rules and the transport binding cannot be finalised without approved protocol/port.

column3: Provide each DCS platform with its exact OPC A&E (and DA where used) server product and version (Honeywell, Emerson, Yokogawa, Foxboro, Matrikon).
column4: Connector compatibility and certified versions must be verified per OEM before commitment.

column3: Foxboro does not expose OPC A&E like the other DCS. Confirm the alternative integration is via SQL, provide the source schema, and confirm a synchronization time <= 5 s is achievable and acceptable.
column4: Foxboro is the exception case; the SQL path and 5-second sync target must be validated against the actual schema.

column3: For Sequence of Events: must the CAS preserve the original millisecond timestamp generated at the lowest-level controller, and do all legacy OPC A&E servers actually pass this granular SOE timestamp (versus server-receive time)?
column4: SOE fidelity depends on the source. If servers only pass receive-time, true ms SOE cannot be guaranteed and expectations must be reset.

column3: What time-synchronization source/standard (NTP / PTP) is used across the sites so cross-vendor SOE ordering is coherent?
column4: Consistent time base is prerequisite for merging SOE from different OEMs into one ordered table.

column3: Are alarm normalization / formatting rules required when consolidating events from disparate OEMs into one unified real-time alarm table (priority mapping, condition naming, area/asset model)?
column4: Defines the normalization layer in the edge/central tier and the effort to map each OEM's model.

column3: When a new DCS alarm/tag is added, must the CAS alarm database and banners update automatically (auto-discovery), or is manual reconfiguration acceptable? (Spec row 40.)
column4: Auto-discovery vs manual config materially changes design complexity and lifecycle effort.

column3: Future ABB and GE OPC A&E/DA connectivity is listed as upcoming. Confirm whether these must be included now (and priced) or are optional future phases.
column4: Determines whether ABB/GE connectors are in the current commercial scope.

column3: Confirm whether OPC DA is genuinely required, or whether OPC A&E alone meets the alarm/event scope (spec row 39 prefers no OPC-DA exposure).
column4: Avoids unnecessary DA polling load if A&E covers the requirement.

column3: Peak alarm flood rate: expected worst-case alarms/second per site and aggregate at the IOC.
column4: Drives edge buffer, broker throughput and database write sizing for the worst case.

column3: Steady-state and average event rates per site and aggregate.
column4: Baseline capacity and storage growth planning.

column3: Concurrent users: number of simultaneous operator / engineer / viewer sessions at peak.
column4: Sizes the web/UI tier and concurrent-session licensing.

column3: Historical retention: required online retention period for alarms/events, plus archive and purge policy.
column4: Sizes the historical store and defines archival design.

column3: Confirm the near-real-time update target — the spec states 5-10 s, while other sections imply <= 5 s — and the acceptable end-to-end latency from DCS event to banner.
column4: Resolves a conflicting requirement and sets the performance SLA the design must meet.

column3: Total tag/condition count per OPC server and aggregate across all sites.if available
column4: Capacity planning for subscriptions, buffers and the alarm database.

column3: With AVEVA integration potentially descoped, will PDO / Yokogawa supply the dedicated hardware and monitors for the standalone operator stations, or must client hardware be included in our offer?
column4: Decides whether client hardware is a cost line in the commercial offer.

column3: Exactly how many standalone operator stations are required across the Central Control Room and the IOC?
column4: Sizes client deployment, licensing and commissioning effort.

column3: Preferred client deployment: a centralized web-based UI via standard browsers (Edge/Chrome), or a thick-client install? (We recommend web based.)
column4: Sets the UI delivery model; Web based reduces per-station maintenance and avoids ActiveX/DCOM concerns.

column3: If AVEVA remains in scope: must the banner be embedded as an ActiveX / HTML5 control inside the existing Wonderware HMI, or run as a standalone window?
column4: Embedding constraints (especially ActiveX) significantly affect UI architecture.

column3: Is Single Sign-On (e.g. Active Directory / LDAP) required for operator authentication, and which identity provider must we integrate with?
column4: Defines authentication integration and the RBAC/role-based filter presets (spec row 28).

column3: Confirm the required integrations and direction for PI and/or SQL (read alarm data out only, or also write into CAS).
column4: Defines the integration interfaces and data-flow direction with the historian/database layer.

column3: Baseera, Nibras and other PDO third-party software — confirm the interface method (PI, SQL, REST API) and which systems are in scope.
column4: Defines outbound integration adapters required for PDO's wider toolset.

column3: Is an open API required to expose commands/control to and from the IOC platform (spec row 30), and over which protocol (REST / OPC UA)?
column4: Determines whether a published API layer is in scope and its protocol.

column3: Confirm the CCTV / RDP integration referenced under 'open architecture' (spec row 33) — is this within CAS scope or handled display-side only?
column4: Clarifies whether multimedia/RDP panes are a CAS deliverable.

column3: Required availability / RPO / RTO for the central alarm database and broker (HA cluster, N+1, geo-redundancy)?
column4: Sets the redundancy design and infrastructure count.

column3: Confirm the store-and-forward buffer depth required at the edge — the maximum outage duration to survive with zero data loss — so local disk can be sized.
column4: Directly sizes edge buffer storage for the mandated store-and-forward capability.

column3: On reconnection, must backfilled events be merged into history in correct SOE order using original timestamps? Confirm acceptable backfill behaviour.
column4: Defines backfill correctness rules and history reconciliation logic.

column3: Is broker redundancy / clustering required, and is a DMZ-resident broker bridge to the IOC acceptable?
column4: Confirms broker HA topology and placement relative to the DMZ.

column3: Must licensing cover the future ABB / GE connectors and additional sites beyond the initial 74?
column4: Determines whether future expansion is pre-licensed or chargeable later.

column3: Confirm currency, payment milestones, and the warranty / support period expected for the commercial offer.
column4: Required to structure the commercial proposal.

column3: Are locally certified resources required in the Sultanate of Oman for support and future expansion (spec row 64), and is In-Country Value (ICV) a scoring criterion?
column4: Affects resourcing model, partnerships and bid scoring.

column3: Confirm the required implementation timeline and any mandated milestones, including FAT/SAT requirements (spec row 65).
column4: Sets the project schedule and acceptance gates.
